content:
Former MLB star-turned-Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira (R-Texas) whiffed in the House office lottery on Tuesday, and he was still a good sport about it anyway.

Teixeira, a first baseman with the 2009 World Series champion New York Yankees, pulled the 105th of 105 total chips, making him the last of the incoming freshman lawmakers to select his office space.

Video shared by Teixeira on X shows the Yankees great reacting like his team won a big game as he holds the chip while raising his hands in the air as a room full of newly elected congress members erupts in cheers and applause.

Teixeira proceeded to go around the room and high-five dozens of his future colleagues.

“I consider it an honor to have the last pick of offices and let all my fellow freshmen go ahead of me,” wrote Teixeira alongside the clip.

“As Matthew 19:30 reminds us, ‘But many who are first will be last, and the last first.’”

The former slugger — who has stood behind Donald Trump’s immigration policies and was endorsed by the president on the campaign trail — defeated Democrat Kristin Hook earlier this month in a race to succeed retiring Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas).

“Sometimes you prepare, you put the work in, and it’s just not your night,” he said.

“Today wasn’t my day, but no, I’m gonna have fun with this. I absolutely will. Someone had to be 105, and so I’m happy it was me.”

He told Roll Call that the office selection was low on his priority list and said he’s “serving” the rest of his freshman class by picking the “worst” office.
